svg.title: Agent failure lab: a hand-written tool-calling agent over three-way invoice matching, run fifty times
svg.desc: A harness in one repository runs ten cases five times each. Before every attempt it restores a seed payment history, then starts an agent loop of about 130 lines with a hard limit of twelve steps. The loop sends the conversation and nine tool schemas to an OpenAI model, which answers with tool calls. Six lookup tools read five JSON fixture files; three terminal tools end the run, and only approve for payment writes anything. Every event is appended to a trace file and synced to disk, and a script reads the fifty traces into a per-case table. Results: 44 of 50 correct, 4 of 50 false approvals, 8 of 10 cases with full agreement. Finding one: in case 7 all five attempts made the same calls and received the same results, including a vendor lookup error, yet one escalated and four approved. Finding two: the model supplied the same idempotency key on every approval, but the payment tool wrote the key and never read it. After an injected crash the restart did not pay twice, only because the model chose to check for a prior payment, and it ended in reject, which is wrong.
svg.text: A hand-written tool-calling agent over three-way invoice matching, run fifty times to count how it fails
Each case has an expected outcome
Seed file restored before each run
One line per event, synced to disk
Chooses which tool to call next
Each has trace files behind it in the repo.
Case 7: invoice, PO and receipt agree. The vendor lookup fails.
Five attempts, the same five calls, byte-identical results
The error was in the transcript at the moment it approved.
2 - A stable key that guaranteed nothing
Six approvals of the same invoice, fresh context each time.
The model built the same idempotency key every time
Writes the key into the payment record. Never reads it.
A key only protects if something on the write path checks it.
Per case - correct outcomes out of five
Case 7 produced all four false approvals. Case 2 over-escalated twice.
After an injected crash and restart
Nothing required that check, and the key played no part.
Preconditions go in the tool, not the prompt.
Actions with side effects need an already-done outcome.
Reset state before every run, or the numbers mislead.
Report agreement across runs, not one run's accuracy.
run.py picks a case and an attempt, restores the seed payment history and starts the loop.
The loop sends the conversation and the nine tool schemas to the model.
The model answers with tool calls - typically four lookups in a single turn.
Each call is dispatched. Results go back to the model as data, and so do errors.
A terminal tool ends the run. Only approve_for_payment writes: one record in the payment history.
Every model call, tool call and result is appended to the run's trace file and synced to disk.
analyse.py reads the fifty traces and builds the per-case table.
